speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings following a tympanoplasty. To help me pinpoint the issue, how would you describe the character of this pain, and does it trigger when you touch the outer ear or insert anything?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain you describe occurring while eating strongly suggests irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve; does the pain also radiate to your jaw or temple, and do you notice any stiffness there? Additionally, have you noticed any swelling, redness, or drainage at the surgical site on your right ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (post-tympanoplasty). The combination of shooting ear pain triggered by chewing, the history of recent ear surgery, and discomfort with earrings suggests irritation or entrapment of the auriculotemporal nerve, likely due to scar tissue formation affecting the nerve near the zygomatic arch or within the ear canal.
